TODO: FIND GOOD DATA - wide to long format (chest x-ray data?) - line plot (ebola cases?) # Data tidying ## Tidy data > "Tidy datasets are easy to manipulate, model and visualise, and have a specific structure: each variable is a column, each observation is a row, and each type of observational unit is a table." > > Tidy Data, . . . **Note:** "easy to manipulate" = "straightforward to manipulate" ## Goal Visualize StatSci majors over the years! ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w04-03-tidy_files/figure-revealjs/plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: ## Data {.smaller} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} degrees ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 17 degree_type `2011` `2012` `2013` `2014` `2015` `2016` `2017` 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 # ℹ 9 more variables: `2018` , `2019` , `2020` , # `2021` , `2022` , `2023` , `2024` , # `2025` , `2026` ``` ::: ::: ::: incremental - The first column (variable) is the `degree`: ::: small - AB (Bachelor of Arts) - AB2 (Bachelor of Arts, 2nd major) - BS (Bachelor of Science) - BS2 (Bachelor of Science, 2nd major) ::: - The remaining columns show the number of students graduating with that major in a given academic year from 2011 to 2026.
If you double major, your first major determines the degree you will earn. For example, if you double major in English and Statistical Science, you will graduate with a BA degree, because your first major (English) offers the BA degree. If, on the other hand, you were to make Statistical Science the first major, you would have the option to complete either the BA or the BS degree, since Statistical Science offers a BS as well as a BA track.
::: ## Let's plan! {.smaller} Review the goal plot and sketch the data frame needed to create it. What would go inside `aes` when we call `ggplot`? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w04-03-tidy_files/figure-revealjs/plot2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: ## The Goal {.smaller .nostretch} We want to write code that starts something like this: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(degrees, aes(x = year, y = count, color = degree_type)) + ... ``` ::: . . .
But our data are not in the right format :( ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} degrees ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 17 degree_type `2011` `2012` `2013` `2014` `2015` `2016` `2017` 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 # ℹ 9 more variables: `2018` , `2019` , `2020` , # `2021` , `2022` , `2023` , `2024` , # `2025` , `2026` ``` ::: ::: ## The Challenge {.smaller .nostretch} ::: columns ::: {.column width="70%"} ***How do we go from this ....*** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 x 16 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 4 4 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 0 0 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 21 26 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 8 8 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="30%"} ***.... to this??*** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 60 x 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 11 AB 2021 0 12 AB 2022 0 13 AB 2023 2 14 AB 2024 1 15 AB 2025 0 16 AB 2026 2 17 AB2 2011 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Pivot ## `pivot_longer()` {.smaller .scrollable} ::: columns ::: {.column width="65%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 x 16 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 4 4 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 0 0 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 21 26 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 8 8 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.task .fragment} Pivot the `degrees` data frame *longer* such that each row represents a degree type / year combination. `year` and `count` (number of graduates for that year) are columns in the resulting data frame. ::: ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ⟶ ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 60 x 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 11 AB 2021 0 12 AB 2022 0 13 AB 2023 2 14 AB 2024 1 15 AB 2025 0 16 AB 2026 2 17 AB2 2011 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## `pivot_longer()` {.smaller .scrollable} ::: columns ::: {.column width="65%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 x 16 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 4 4 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 0 0 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 21 26 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 8 8 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.task .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} degrees |> pivot_longer( cols = ___________________ , names_to = _______________ , values_to = ______________ ) ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ⟶ ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 60 x 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 11 AB 2021 0 12 AB 2022 0 13 AB 2023 2 14 AB 2024 1 15 AB 2025 0 16 AB 2026 2 17 AB2 2011 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Why? What should it be? ::: ::: fragment ::: incremental - It's a character (`chr`) variable since the information came from the columns of the original data frame. - R cannot know that these character strings represent years. - The variable type should be numeric. ::: ::: ::: ::: ## `pivot_longer()` again {.smaller .scrollable} ::: question This time, also make sure `year` is a numerical variable in the resulting data frame. ::: ::: columns ::: {.column width = "50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} degrees |> pivot_longer( cols = -degree_type, values_to = "count", names_to = "year" ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width = "50%" } ::: ::: ## `pivot_longer()` again {.smaller .scrollable} ::: question This time, also make sure `year` is a numerical variable in the resulting data frame. ::: ::: columns ::: {.column width = "50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|6"} degrees |> pivot_longer( cols = -degree_type, values_to = "count", names_to = "year", names_transform = as.numeric ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width = "50%" .fragment} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 64 × 3 degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 # ℹ 54 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Pivot Wider ## We pivotted longer... what about wider? {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="65%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 x 16 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 4 4 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 0 0 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 21 26 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 8 8 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.task .fragment} Can we go the other direction? ::: ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ⟵ ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 60 x 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 11 AB 2021 0 12 AB 2022 0 13 AB 2023 2 14 AB 2024 1 15 AB 2025 0 16 AB 2026 2 17 AB2 2011 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## We pivotted longer... what about wider? {.smaller} ::: columns ::: {.column width="65%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 x 16 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 1 AB 2 2 4 1 3 6 3 4 4 2 AB2 0 1 0 0 4 4 1 0 0 3 BS 5 9 4 13 10 17 24 21 26 4 BS2 2 6 1 0 5 6 6 8 8 ``` ::: ::: ::: task ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} degrees_longer |> pivot_wider( names_from = ____________ , values_from = ___________ , ) ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ⟵ ::: ::: {.column width="30%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 60 x 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` degree_type year count 1 AB 2011 2 2 AB 2012 2 3 AB 2013 4 4 AB 2014 1 5 AB 2015 3 6 AB 2016 6 7 AB 2017 3 8 AB 2018 4 9 AB 2019 4 10 AB 2020 1 11 AB 2021 0 12 AB 2022 0 13 AB 2023 2 14 AB 2024 1 15 AB 2025 0 16 AB 2026 2 17 AB2 2011 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## {.smaller} ![](../img/tidyr-pivoting.gif){fig-align="center"} ## Recap: Pivot {.smaller} ::: incremental - ***When should you pivot?*** If all of the data you need is in your data frame, but the columns you need don't exist, there is a good chance it's time to pivot! - ***Wide and long:*** Data sets can't be labeled as *wide* or *long* but they can be made *wider* or *longer* for a certain analysis that requires a certain format - ***Pivot longer - data type:*** When pivoting longer, variable names that turn into values are characters by default. If you need them to be in another format, you need to explicitly make that transformation, which you can do so within the `pivot_longer()` function. ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
